h1: Driver's License Help in El Paso
intro: Losing your license in El Paso means losing the way to work, school and Fort Bliss. Attorney Robert Navar helps drivers figure out why the license was suspended or blocked, get an occupational license to drive legally in the meantime, and clear the path to full reinstatement.
summary: A Texas license is suspended or blocked for a short list of reasons: too many points, a DWI or refusal, no insurance after a crash, unpaid tickets through an OMNI hold, or child-support and other administrative actions.
An occupational driver's license under Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L lets you drive for work, school and household needs while a suspension runs.
Driving on a suspended license is its own offense — DWLI, Transportation Code 521.457 — and it extends the suspension. Get the ODL first.
The consultation is free. Schedule an appointment or call 915-503-1600 and bring your DPS notice.

sections.heading: Why Texas Suspends or Blocks El Paso Drivers' Licenses
paragraphs: Most license problems we see in El Paso fall into a handful of buckets. The first is points. Texas still runs a points system for suspension purposes — two points per moving-violation conviction, three if there was a crash — and DPS can suspend a driver who collects four moving convictions in 12 months or seven in 24.

The second bucket is an administrative suspension: a DWI arrest, a breath or blood test refusal, a crash without insurance, or a medical or child-support action. These have fixed lengths set by statute and start whether or not the criminal case has been decided. The third bucket is not technically a suspension at all. An OMNI hold under Transportation Code Chapter 706 means a court reported an unpaid ticket or missed date, and DPS will not renew the license until the court clears it. Each has a different fix, and the first thing we do in a consultation is pull your DPS record and figure out which one you actually have — many drivers have two or three stacked on top of each other.

sections.heading: The Occupational Driver's License: Driving Legally During a Suspension
paragraphs: An occupational driver's license (ODL) is a court order under Transportation Code 521.241 and the sections that follow that lets a suspended driver operate a non-commercial vehicle for work, school, and essential household duties. We file a petition in the appropriate El Paso County court, attach proof of SR-22 insurance and a certified driving record, and ask the judge to sign an order setting the hours, days and purposes you may drive. In most cases the signed order itself works as a temporary license while DPS issues the card.

The ODL is the most useful tool for an El Paso driver with a suspension, because the alternative is driving anyway. A driving while license invalid ticket is a Class C offense the first time and can become a Class B with a prior or a crash — and every DWLI conviction extends the suspension. Our original occupational license page is still online with the paperwork checklist.

sections.heading: The Path Back to a Full License
paragraphs: Reinstatement depends on what caused the problem. For an OMNI hold, the court must send DPS a clearance after the ticket is resolved; our OMNI hold removal page explains how we resolve the underlying case — often with a dismissal or deferred disposition so it adds no points — and push the clearance through so you can renew. For a points suspension, the suspension period has to run, DPS reinstatement fees have to be paid, and in the meantime we fight any new ticket so nothing adds to the count. For a DWI or refusal suspension, the ODL carries you through the period.

A few things make reinstatement slower than it needs to be: an SR-22 that lapses mid-suspension and restarts the clock, a second court's OMNI hold nobody noticed, or an unpaid reinstatement fee sitting in the DPS system. We check all three before telling a client the license is clear. If you already picked up a no driver's license or DWLI citation while suspended, those are usually negotiable once a valid ODL is in hand.

sections.heading: Which Page Do You Need?
paragraphs: If your license is already suspended and you need to drive, go to occupational driver's license. If DPS said it cannot renew because of a court hold, go to OMNI hold removal. If you were ticketed for driving on a suspended license, see driving while license invalid. If you want to understand how close you are to a suspension before it happens, read the Texas points system explained and then fight the pending ticket through our traffic tickets hub.

faqs.q: Can I get an occupational license in El Paso if my license is suspended for DWI?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. There may be a waiting period depending on prior offenses, and the court may require an ignition interlock, but an ODL is routinely granted for DWI-related suspensions. See our occupational driver's license page for the details.

faqs.q: What happens if I drive while my license is suspended?
faqs.a: You can be cited for driving while license invalid under Transportation Code 521.457. A first offense is a Class C misdemeanor; with a prior conviction, a crash or no insurance it can be a Class B with possible jail. A conviction also extends the suspension. An ODL avoids all of that.

faqs.q: My license is fine but DPS won't renew it. What is going on?
faqs.a: That is almost always an OMNI hold — a court reported an unpaid ticket or missed appearance. The ticket has to be resolved and the court has to send DPS a clearance. We handle both; see OMNI hold removal.

faqs.q: How much does license help cost?
faqs.a: The consultation is free. An occupational license is a flat fee quoted after we see your record, plus the court filing fee and your SR-22. Clearing an OMNI hold is priced like any ticket: $59 in El Paso Municipal Court, $69 in JP and the smaller city courts, plus $35 if there is a warrant.
